summary: A cardholder makes purchases during a billing cycle, receives a statement with a due date, and then submits a payment after that due date for less than the required minimum. The scenario is designed to exercise the late-payment/default path while also showing that the account stayed within the credit limit and that the prior-cycle grace-period condition was not satisfied.
assumptions: The billing cycle closes on 2025-03-31 and the statement shows a New Balance of $600.00 with a payment due date of 2025-04-25.
Under the contract formula, the minimum payment for a $600.00 New Balance is $18.00 (3% of $600.00), which is greater than $15.00.
A payment of $10.00 is intentionally posted on 2025-04-28, after the due date, so the minimum payment obligation is not met on time.

The prior statement was not paid in full by its due date, so the contractual grace-period condition for new purchases is not satisfied in this archetype; a notice event is included referencing clause.6.grace_period to record that this obligation is treated as unmet/not triggered for the late-payment narrative.
The account remains below the $1,000.00 credit limit throughout the scenario, so the credit-limit obligation is satisfied.

A due_check event is used to test whether the required minimum payment was made by the due date; it references the minimum-payment obligation clause even though the outcome is breach rather than performance.

metadata.message: Prior statement was not paid in full by its due date, so no purchase grace period applies for this cycle.
Late payment fee may be assessed because payment was late and below minimum.
